Subject: Post-call: Performance & SLO qualification — Private/VPC networking

Hi John —

Thanks again for the time today — good kickoff. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on what we need to validate performance in your Private/VPC deployment: 

Summary of customer SLOs we discussed:
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end (app -> model) <= 50 ms for small prompt flows; p95 <= 150 ms for long-form streaming/assistant sessions
- Throughput: sustained 500 requests/min baseline, spike to 2,000 requests/min for 10m bursts
- Concurrency: 150 concurrent interactive sessions (typical session = streaming, ~30 tokens/sec)
- Streaming: low-latency token streaming required; partial-response delivery (chunked) acceptable

What we need from Acme to finalize sizing and network path validation:
1) Network topology for VPC peering / VPN / Direct Connect (diagram or notes)
2) Any egress filtering, NAT gateway constrains, or proxying for outbound connections to Redwood endpoints
3) Internal latency budget (app -> edge / app -> internet egress) and any requirements for TLS termination
4) A short pcap/traceroute of a representative request path (app host -> Redwood egress IP) if possible

I’ve attached a short SLO template (redwood-slo-template.pdf) you can fill and return; that’ll help our capacity planning and the tech deep-dive.

Next steps:
- John: share network details + pcap if available (ideally before Thu 25 Jun)
- We’ll schedule a 60m tech deep-dive the week of Jun 29 to align on peering/egress and run a basic perf model
- I’ll loop in Engineering (Aditya, Dev) to validate streaming and concurrency assumptions once we get the pcap

Thanks — looking forward to getting this dialed in.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few notes from our side and I’ve attached an annotated pcap (network-trace-annotated.pcap) showing a few representative flows. High-level:

Environment notes:
- We’re running in AWS us-west-2 with a Transit Gateway. We currently peer to a vendor edge (Egress NAT in a centralized VPC) and will likely use a Site-to-Site VPN to connect to Redwood Private control plane if we go that route.
- Egress constraints: company-wide outbound proxy and strict egress rules; we’ll need to open specific IPs/ports or go via an agreed peering approach.
- TLS: Termination is at our edge — mutual TLS is an option if Redwood supports client certs for private deployments.

Internal latency budgets:
- App -> backend model endpoint (internal): target p95 <= 45 ms (this is aggressive but required for our UX)
- Backend -> external egress: commonly 5-12 ms; across our transit gateway + vendor edge we’ve seen 15-25 ms to similar partners in the region

Streaming requirements:
- We need token-level streaming for the assistant use case. Ideally, partial token delivery within 100 ms of generation for short tokens; acceptable p95 <= 150 ms for longer segments.

I attached the pcap and a couple of notes in the file. Let me know if you need a packet capture from a different hop — we can coordinate with SRE.

John

John —

Appreciate the details and the pcap — that’s very helpful. A few clarifications from our side and proposed next steps: 

Clarifications / Redwood notes:
- Mutual TLS: yes, Redwood Private supports mTLS for control plane and can be configured for data plane peering; we’ll bring config examples to the tech deep-dive.
- IPs & peering: for Dedicated/Private we can support a few deployment options: (1) VPC peering / Transit Gateway attachment, (2) Site-to-Site VPN with static routes, (3) Direct Connect/partner interconnect. If egress proxying is mandatory on your side, we’ll need a stable outbound IP/range or a peering approach for stable egress paths.
- Streaming performance: our serving runtime supports token-level streaming. For the numbers you provided we’d expect to meet p95 <= 50 ms for short prompt flows when the end-to-end network is within ~30 ms one-way; long-form sessions will be higher depending on token size and model latency. We’ll validate specifics in the tech call.

Sizing assumptions we’ll validate (please confirm):
- Baseline throughput: 500 req/min (~8.3 req/s) with 2,000 req/min spikes
- Concurrency: 150 concurrent streaming sessions (assume average 30 tokens/sec per session)
- Model mix: 70% short prompts (low token count), 30% streaming assistant sessions

Action items / calendar:
- Can you share traceroute from app host -> Redwood egress IP and indicate whether the pcap was collected before or after your outbound proxy? (helps us interpret the hop timings).
- Let’s schedule a 60m tech deep-dive: proposed slots Tue 30 Jun 09:00 PT or Wed 1 Jul 11:00 PT. Please confirm preferred slot.
- I’ll create an internal Engineering ticket and include Aditya/Dev to run a quick perf model from our side using your pcap.

If that all sounds right I’ll send a calendar invite and our tech checklist (network_ports.txt, cert exchange procedure) ahead of the call.

Best,
Marissa

Team — forwarding Acme thread and annotated pcap. Quick internal notes: 

- John’s p95 target (app->model <=45 ms) is aggressive but potentially achievable if we (a) terminate TLS as close to their app (peering/edge) and (b) avoid extra NAT/egress hops.
- Streaming: our runtime supports sub-50ms p95 for short tokens on optimized kernels, but that assumes network RTT + minimal queuing. Need to validate per-token serialization overhead for their session sizes.
- Ask: can Aditya/ Jonas run the pcap through our internal perf model and estimate expected p95s for (i) VPC peering case, (ii) Site-to-Site VPN case with an extra 15-25ms hop? Also note egress proxy could add variable latency.

I’ll coordinate with Marissa to schedule the tech deep-dive once we have the perf estimates.

Thanks,
